questions.question: In broad geographic usage, Sub-Saharan Africa refers mainly to areas south of which desert?
choices: Gobi
Sahara
Atacama
Thar

questions.question: What is the Sahel?
choices: A semiarid transition zone along the Sahara's southern edge
A permanent ice sheet covering central Africa
A coral island chain east of Madagascar
A mountain range along the southern Cape

questions.question: Which large river basin is associated with central African tropical rainforest?
choices: Niger Basin
Orange Basin
Zambezi Basin
Congo Basin

questions.question: Which island lies off Africa's southeastern coast in the Indian Ocean?
choices: Sri Lanka
Cuba
Madagascar
Iceland

questions.question: Which feature is associated with eastern Africa's tectonic activity?
choices: East African Rift
Great Dividing Range
Appalachian Mountains
Amazon Basin

questions.question: Which river forms a major inland delta in Botswana?
choices: Congo
Okavango
Niger
Nile

questions.question: What vegetation pattern is typical of a tropical savanna?
choices: Dense evergreen forest with no seasonal dry period
Low Arctic vegetation over widespread permafrost
Grassland with scattered trees
Permanent snowfields with no growing season

questions.question: Why can rainfall variability strongly affect Sahelian farming and herding?
choices: The region receives abundant rainfall every day
All farming uses unlimited underground water
The region is entirely covered by glaciers
Water availability is limited and can change substantially between years

questions.question: How can higher elevation affect climate in the Ethiopian Highlands?
choices: It can produce cooler conditions than nearby lowlands
It makes all rainfall disappear throughout the year
It removes seasonal differences in sunlight
It guarantees the same climate as the Arctic coast

questions.question: Why can transport links be especially important to landlocked African economies?
choices: Landlocked countries cannot sell manufactured goods
Access to overseas trade often depends on routes through neighboring states
Every landlocked country has the same climate
National borders prevent all cross-border road construction

questions.question: How have some colonial-era borders affected African political geography?
choices: They made all societies culturally identical
They followed every existing language boundary precisely
They ended all local political organization
They sometimes divided communities or grouped distinct populations within one state

questions.question: Why is a single description of Sub-Saharan Africa's economy inadequate?
choices: All countries depend on the same export
Economic activities are unaffected by geography
The region includes varied farming, manufacturing, mining, and service economies
Only one urban center exists in the region

questions.question: Why can reliance on one major commodity export create economic risk?
choices: Changes in its world price can strongly affect national earnings
A commodity's price remains fixed forever
Commodity exporters cannot engage in any domestic trade
Export income is unrelated to international demand

questions.question: What challenge can rapid city growth create?
choices: The permanent disappearance of rural settlement
Greater demand for housing, transport, water, and jobs
The automatic elimination of all public-service costs
The end of economic connections between city and countryside

questions.question: How can soil degradation affect agricultural livelihoods?
choices: It increases every crop's yield permanently
It makes rainfall timing irrelevant
It prevents any need for land management
It can reduce productivity and increase pressure on usable land

questions.question: Which climate comparison is most accurate for the Congo Basin and much of the Sahel?
choices: Both have identical year-round Arctic climates
The Sahel is generally wetter than the Congo Basin
The Congo Basin is generally more humid; the Sahel is generally drier
Both regions lack seasonal variation in water availability

questions.question: A regional rainfall map shows a broad dry-to-wet transition south of the Sahara. Which conclusion is most reasonable?
choices: Environmental zones cross political borders and change gradually
Each national border causes an abrupt climate change
Every country south of the Sahara is a desert
Rainfall is unrelated to regional farming patterns

questions.question: A mining town grows while metal prices are high, then loses jobs when prices fall. Which relationship does this illustrate?
choices: Latitude directly determines wages
Global commodity markets can affect local livelihoods
Mining towns are independent of outside demand
Urban growth guarantees permanent employment

questions.question: Which evidence would best challenge the stereotype that Sub-Saharan Africa is entirely rural?
choices: A map showing the locations of major mineral deposits
A table of annual rainfall for several farming districts
Maps and population data for cities such as Lagos and Nairobi
A description of crop production in a rural district

questions.question: A conservation plan protects habitat but affects nearby farming communities. What should planners examine?
choices: Only income expected from visiting tourists
Only changes in national export totals
Only the size of the protected area's administrative staff
Both ecological benefits and effects on local livelihoods
